glance: Customized hormone therapy for menopause symptoms, monitored with regular labs.

signs.heading: Common symptoms
signs.intro: Menopause usually arrives in the late 40s to early 50s, around 51 on average, when the ovaries stop producing estrogen.

basics.heading: Why estrogen matters
paras: Estrogen does more than regulate cycles. It helps maintain bone, preserves collagen in the skin, and keeps blood vessel walls and the vaginal lining elastic.

As levels fall, the risks of heart disease, bone loss and osteoporosis, vaginal atrophy, and urinary incontinence rise, and skin can become drier and thinner. Hormone therapy aims to restore levels, ease symptoms, and protect long-term health.
Hormone therapy is not right for everyone. Dr. Khan reviews your history, risks, and goals with you before recommending it.

options.name: Injections
options.text: Dosed at regular intervals in the office or at home.

options.name: Patch or gel
options.text: Applied to the skin daily or on a set schedule.

options.name: Pellet therapy
options.text: Bioidentical hormones in a rice-sized pellet placed under the skin, releasing a steady dose.

faq: For many women it is a reasonable option, but benefits and risks depend on your age, health history, and timing. Dr. Khan reviews them with you before starting.
Hormones that are chemically identical to the ones your body makes. Pellet therapy uses bioidentical hormones.
